newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa prime rate seen cut within six months.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa prime rate seen cut within six months.

text.p: South Africa's prime interest rate will most likely decline by 0.75 percentage points to 19.5 percent within the next six months, WorldGroup Banking said in its latest monthly interest rate forecast.
Economists participating in the forecast expected the prime rate, currently at 20.25 percent, to fall further to 19 percent by March 1998.

On the money market, the three month bankers' acceptances rate is expected to fall 25 points by June 1997, while the most likely scenario for the 12 month NCD rate sees a 65-point decline in the next quarter to 15.90 percent.
The 90-day BA rate is currently trading between 15.80 to 16.00 percent. Twelve month NCD rates were last between 16.55 to 16.60 percent offered.

On the bond market, the Eskom 168 stock is expected to decline to 15.04 percent within the next three months and to fall further to 14.59 percent by September and 13.99 percent in the next twelve months.
The stock was last at a 15.20 percent yield.
Four economists -- Absa's Adam Jacobs, Transnet's Ulrich Joubert, Kau Msimango of Iscor and Helmo Preuss of Forecaster Ecosa -- took part in the survey.

The economists said the low level of foreign exchange reserves remained a concern although this was tempered by the expectation of an inflow of 5.5 billion rand in May from the sale of state telecommunications utility Telkom in March.
But they said the majority of foreign investment remained short-term and therefore potentially speculative -- a concern which was compounded by South Africa's poor international credit rating.
